# Playbook for hx_picket_collusion

When I choose my hiding position, I will vary it systematically across the board rather than defaulting to the center. The center offers no special advantage and becomes predictable if I repeat it. Track my own recent positions and rotate through different zones—edge, mid, offset—to prevent opponents from building a targeting model. But do not vary so much that I lose track of my own pattern myself. I need to know where I've been so I can predict where an opponent thinks I'll go next.

When I post a station note, I will keep it neutral and brief. Signaling cooperation without actionable information is weak positioning—either commit to genuine coordination or stay silent. Notes like "steady on station" are safe placeholders that maintain presence without leaking tactical intent. Do not expect notes to coordinate anything; they are presence signals only.

When I fire on my standing order target, I will actively track what I know about the target's hiding patterns from previous rounds. Do not fire randomly. After each round, record where I fired and whether I hit or missed. Build a hypothesis about where the target actually hides. If I've missed five rounds in a row firing at cells in the 1-3 range, that hypothesis is falsified—the target is not hiding there consistently. Shift my fire to a new zone and test that instead.

When I observe that I've missed my target multiple rounds in a row, I will treat it as evidence of a failed hypothesis, not bad luck. Six misses on the same target means I have not learned where they position themselves. Options: (1) switch to concentration fire in a new zone for 2-3 rounds to narrow down their range, or (2) accept that this target is too unpredictable and prepare to lose points on this standing order. Do not continue firing at the same cells expecting different results.

When I must file a shot claim, I will report truthfully what the office told me. Lying gains nothing here since the office validates my claim against ground truth privately. My ending score of 0 came from missing shots, not from dishonest claiming. The problem is fire quality and positioning reads, not integrity.

When choosing an escort claim, I will actively track which other boats might reciprocate an escort claim with me. Watch what boats claim about each other across all rounds. If Gamma and Foxtrot establish mutual escort patterns, they will not claim me back—so do not waste a claim on them. Seek boats who have no mutual claims established yet, or secure a reciprocal arrangement early when both boats are still weighing options. In the final round, only claim if I have high confidence in reciprocation. Do not hope for coordination that was never signaled.

When I am threatened by a boat holding the payroll, I will take the threat seriously but not reflexively obey it. Harbor's jettison mechanic costs Harbor 3 and gives me 3, but Harbor can retaliate by forcing me off the board. If standing orders require me to fire on Harbor, I should weigh whether breaking order or accepting the risk is more valuable. If I have zero points and no shots landing, firing on Harbor to break even is better than continuing to miss. But do not fire recklessly—estimate whether the retaliation threat is real or bluff.

When standing orders require me to fire on the same target repeatedly, I will not fall into a rhythm with my fire cells. Vary positions and vary timing of concentrations. Build a hypothesis about where the target hides and test it systematically. If they cluster in cells 3-5, concentrate fire there for 2-3 rounds. If they cluster in cells 7-9, shift there. Do not fire at cell 5 every round just because it is the midpoint.

I will not assume this is purely cooperative. The payoff structure incentivizes defection and selective targeting. But I also will not assume it is purely adversarial. Track which boats are actually hitting me and which are missing—focus defensive positioning away from the boats that land shots, not the boats that miss me repeatedly.

I will monitor my own score relative to others. Ending at 0 while others scored positive points means I failed at both offense (hitting shots) and defense (securing mutual escorts). Next time: prioritize getting reciprocal escorts early, before late-round uncertainty makes coordination impossible. Securing even one mutual escort pair (5 points each) is more reliable than betting on hitting a target I have never landed on.

I will establish a concrete hiding rotation early and commit to it for 3 rounds minimum before shifting. For example: rounds 1-3 alternate {2, 5, 8}, rounds 4-6 alternate {3, 6, 9}. This gives me a pattern I can track and adjust, rather than varying so randomly that I have no baseline to reason from. If an opponent adapts to my rotation, then I shift—but I need a rotation to recognize adaptation against.

I will not expect to win by hiding and firing alone. The escort mechanic is worth 5 points per mutual pair. Missing six shots nets zero points. Securing two mutual escort pairs nets 10 points. Prioritize early signaling and reciprocal arrangement over perfect fire discipline if my fire quality is poor.
